intro: Consumer insights help businesses understand what customers need, what they prefer, how they behave, and why they choose one product or brand over another.

Understanding these factors helps businesses see beyond sales numbers and understand the people behind every purchase.

NexGen Market Research helps businesses identify consumer needs, understand buying behaviour, study brand preferences and discover new market opportunities through consumer insights research services.

sections.title: How Does NexGen Conduct Consumer Insights Research?

blocks.text: NexGen follows a structured research process to understand consumer behaviour and convert findings into useful business insights.
Step 1: Define Research Objectives
We first understand the business requirements, target audience, product category, research objectives and key questions that need answers.
Step 2: Identify the Right Consumers
We identify the relevant consumer groups based on factors such as location, age group, income, lifestyle, product usage and buying behaviour.
Step 3: Collect Consumer Data
Depending on the research objective, we use methods such as:
Consumer Surveys: Collect information about preferences, product usage, buying habits and customer opinions.
In-depth Interviews: Speak directly with consumers to understand their experiences, needs and motivations.
Focus Group Discussions: Bring selected consumers together to understand different opinions, preferences and product perceptions.
Observation: Study actual shopping habits and product usage behaviour.
Secondary Research: Review available market information and industry data to understand broader consumer trends.
Step 4: Analyse Consumer Behaviour
We analyse the collected information to identify common patterns, customer preferences, purchase triggers, barriers, brand choices and differences across consumer groups.
Step 5: Deliver Actionable Insights
We present the findings in a structured format, highlighting key consumer segments, important behaviours, unmet needs and potential growth opportunities to support better business decisions.

/solutions/brand-research.title: Brand Research
/solutions/brand-research.headline: Understand How Customers See, Trust and Choose Your Brand.
intro: Brand research helps businesses understand what customers think and feel about their brand, how well they recognise it, how much they trust it and why they choose it over competitors.
A brand is more than its name, logo or advertising. It is shaped by customer experiences, product quality, trust, communication and the value people associate with it.
NexGen Market Research helps businesses understand how their brand is perceived, measure its value in the minds of customers and identify opportunities to improve brand performance through research.

blocks.text: Knowing how many people recognise your brand is not enough. Businesses also need to understand what customers think about it and what makes it different from competitors.
Brand research helps businesses to:
Is the brand known by the intended audience?
What comes to mind spontaneously when people hear the brand name?
Which associations are strong, weak or distinctive?
What drives trust, preference and willingness to recommend?
How does the brand compare with competitors on relevant attributes?
How are perceptions changing over time?
1. Brand Awareness & Recall
Understand how many customers know your brand, recognise its name and remember it when thinking about a particular product or category.
2. Brand Equity
Measure the value a brand holds in the minds of customers. Understand how brand awareness, trust, perceived quality and customer loyalty influence brand preference and choice.
3. Brand Image & Associations
Understand what customers think about your brand and which qualities, feelings and experiences they associate with it.
4. Brand Positioning & Differentiation
Find out how customers see your brand compared to competitors. Identify what makes your brand different and whether its positioning matches customer expectations.
5. Competitive Brand Benchmarking
Compare your brand with competitors on awareness, image, customer preference, trust and other important factors to identify strengths and improvement areas.
6. Brand Tracking & Health Studies
Track brand performance over time by measuring awareness, consideration, preference, usage and customer perceptions. Understand whether your brand image is improving or changing.
7. Brand Architecture Research
Understand how customers view different brands, sub-brands and products within a company. Help businesses maintain a clear identity across their brand portfolio.
8. Brand Repositioning Research
Understand whether your current brand positioning is still relevant to customers. Identify what changes in brand image or identity may help strengthen its market position.
9. Brand Extension Research
Study how customers may respond when an existing brand launches a new product or enters a new category. Understand whether the existing brand name supports the new offering.

intro: Product & Innovation Research helps businesses understand customer needs and test new product ideas, features, and designs before launching them in the market.

Discover : Identifying customer needs and new ideas.
Develop : Developing ideas into products.
Validate : Checking whether a product idea is useful for customers.
Optimise : Making improvements to the product based on feedback.
Launch : Introducing the product to the market.

Depending on the project, quality checks may include location validation, respondent checks, interview review and data consistency checks. The type and extent of verification are agreed according to the project scope.

sections.title: Census and Sample Survey: Understanding the Difference

blocks.text: A census aims to cover every eligible unit within a clearly defined population or area. A sample survey, on the other hand, collects information from selected units and uses the results to understand the larger population.

A census can provide complete coverage only when the target area and eligible units are clearly defined and all required units can be identified and listed. If full coverage is not possible, the actual coverage and limitations should be clearly mentioned in the final report.

blocks.text: NexGen uses different research methods based on the study objectives and the people we need to understand.
1. Focus Group Discussions (FGDs)
Group discussions led by a trained moderator. Participants share their views, experiences and opinions on a specific topic, product or service.
2. In-Depth Interviews (IDIs)
One-to-one conversations that help explore personal experiences, opinions, motivations and decision-making in greater detail. Interviews can be conducted in person or online.
3. Key Informant Interviews (KIIs)
Interviews with people who have relevant knowledge or experience, such as industry experts, professionals, decision-makers and other key stakeholders.
4. Ethnographic Research and Observation
Observing people in their everyday surroundings, such as homes, workplaces and retail stores, to understand their habits, routines and actual behaviour.
5. Shop-Alongs and Accompanied Journeys
Following shoppers during their shopping experience to understand how they select products, compare brands and make purchase decisions.
6. Online Qualitative Discussions
Online discussions and interviews that allow participants to share their views and experiences remotely.
7. Moderation, Transcription and Translation
Support for conducting research sessions, preparing transcripts and translating discussions where required.

/methodologies/mixed-methods.title: Mixed-Methods Research
/methodologies/mixed-methods.headline: Combine Data and Customer Insights for a Clearer Picture.
intro: Numbers can show what is happening, while conversations can help explain why it is happening. Some research questions need both types of information to get a complete understanding.

Mixed-methods research combines quantitative surveys with qualitative interviews, group discussions or other research methods. It helps businesses measure customer opinions and behaviour while also understanding the reasons behind them.
NexGen uses a combination of research methods based on the study objectives, target audience and information required.

blocks.text: The research design depends on what the study needs to find out. Common approaches include:
1. Qualitative Research Followed by Quantitative Research

The study starts with interviews or group discussions to understand the topic. The findings are then used to prepare a survey and measure how common those views or behaviours are among a larger group.
2. Quantitative Research Followed by Qualitative Research
A survey first identifies patterns, differences or unexpected results. Interviews or group discussions are then used to understand the reasons behind those findings.
3. Parallel Qualitative and Quantitative Research
Surveys and qualitative discussions are conducted during the same research period. The findings from both methods are compared to develop a broader understanding of the topic.
4. Multi-Stage Research

The study is completed in stages and may combine secondary research, surveys, interviews and discussions with relevant stakeholders. This approach is useful when the research covers several topics or groups.
Using both research methods can help when a study needs measurable results as well as a deeper understanding of people's views.
It can be useful for:
New Market Entry: Understand market demand, customer needs and buying behaviour before entering a new market.
New Product Launch: Measure product interest and explore customer reactions, expectations and concerns.
Customer Satisfaction: Measure satisfaction levels and understand the reasons behind customer feedback.
Customer Switching: Identify how many customers are changing brands and explore why they are doing so.
Pricing Research: Measure willingness to pay and understand how customers view different prices and offers.
Advertising and Communication: Measure campaign awareness and recall while exploring how people understand the message.
Healthcare and Social Research: Measure awareness, access and outcomes while understanding the experiences of patients, communities and other stakeholders.
Business and Institutional Research: Combine survey findings with interviews to understand the views of professionals and decision-makers.

intro: Manufacturing and industrial research helps businesses understand their markets, customers, suppliers and competitors. It covers areas such as product demand, buying decisions, procurement needs, distribution channels and industry trends.

sections.title: Why Are Data Collection & Fieldwork Important?

blocks.text: Good research depends on the quality of the information collected. Proper fieldwork helps businesses and research organisations:
Reach the right respondents for their studies.
Collect information from different locations and target groups.
Understand customer, business and community needs.
Maintain consistency during surveys and interviews.
Identify incomplete or inconsistent responses.
Get reliable data for research and business decisions.

/data-fieldwork/survey-programming.headline: Turn Research Questionnaires into Ready-to-Use Surveys.
intro: Survey programming is the process of converting a research questionnaire into a digital survey. It includes setting up questions, response options, skip logic, quotas and data checks so respondents can complete the survey correctly.
NexGen provides survey programming support to help research teams prepare and test online questionnaires before data collection.

blocks.text: A well-programmed survey helps collect information in the right format and reduces errors during data collection. It helps to:
Make sure questions appear in the correct order.
Show relevant questions based on previous answers.
Apply sample quotas and screening rules.
Reduce incomplete or incorrect responses.
Make surveys easy to complete on different devices.
Prepare data in the required format for analysis.
NexGen follows the questionnaire and project requirements to build and test digital surveys.
Our process includes:
Questionnaire Review: Understand the questions, research objectives and survey flow.
Survey Scripting: Set up questions, response options and digital survey structure.

Language Setup: Prepare survey versions in the required languages.
Device Testing: Check the survey on mobile phones, tablets and desktops.
Pilot Testing: Test the survey, identify issues and make required changes.
Data Preparation: Export survey data in the agreed format.

/data-fieldwork/translation.title: Translation & Localisation
/data-fieldwork/translation.headline: Making Research Clear and Easy to Understand in Every Language
intro: Translation and localisation help people understand research questions and other content in their own language. It is not just about translating words. The original meaning, context and intent must remain the same so that people can understand the questions and respond correctly.
NexGen supports the translation and review of questionnaires, research documents and business content for different languages and audiences.

blocks.text: Clear language helps people understand what is being asked. Poor translation can change the meaning of a question and affect the quality of responses.
Good translation helps to:
Make questionnaires easy to understand.
Keep the meaning of questions and response options consistent.
Use words and expressions that are familiar to local audiences.
Reduce confusion among survey respondents.
Maintain consistency across different language versions.
Questionnaires and survey instruments
Discussion guides and interview schedules
Research briefs and participant materials
Business reports and presentations
Marketing and communication content
Regional-language research materials
NexGen follows a review process to make sure translated content is clear and keeps the original meaning.
Understand the purpose: We review the content, target audience and context before starting.
Translate the content: We translate the material while keeping its original meaning and intent.
Review language and wording: We check terminology, tone and whether the content is easy for the audience to understand.
Resolve unclear points: We discuss any unclear wording with the client or research team.
Deliver the final version: We provide the translated content in the agreed format.

For research projects, translation also needs to maintain consistency in concepts, rating scales and response options. NexGen can include back-translation or an additional language review when required by the project.

intro: Transcription is the process of converting audio or video recordings into written text. Research interviews and group discussions often contain useful details, opinions and experiences. A written transcript helps keep this information available for review, analysis and reporting.
NexGen provides transcription support for research recordings and other agreed audio or video material.

blocks.text: Recordings can contain important details that may be difficult to capture through notes alone. Transcripts make it easier for research teams to review conversations and refer to what participants have said.
Transcription helps to:
Keep a written record of interviews and discussions.
Review participant responses in detail.
Identify common views, opinions and feedback.
Support research analysis and report preparation.
Refer back to specific responses when required.
Focus group discussions (FGDs) and in-depth interviews (IDIs)
Key informant and expert interviews
Customer and stakeholder calls
Community and beneficiary discussions
Meetings, training sessions and webinars
Recordings in English, Hindi, Hinglish and agreed regional languages, subject to resource availability
NexGen follows a clear process to prepare transcripts from research recordings.
Receive the recordings: Files are shared through an agreed secure channel.
Confirm requirements: We confirm the language, transcript format, level of detail and delivery timeline.
Prepare the transcript: The audio or video recording is converted into written text.
Review the transcript: We check completeness, speaker identification and formatting.
Deliver the files: The final transcript is shared in the agreed format.

NexGen handles recordings and transcripts according to the confidentiality and data-handling requirements agreed for each project. If required, identifying details can be removed from the transcripts.

/data-fieldwork/data-processing.title: Data Processing, Coding & Tabulation
/data-fieldwork/data-processing.headline: Preparing Raw Research Data for Analysis
intro: Data processing is the process of checking, cleaning and organising research data before analysis. Survey responses and other research information may contain missing entries, inconsistent answers or text responses that need to be grouped and coded.
NexGen provides data processing, coding and tabulation services to turn raw research data into structured files that are ready for analysis and reporting.

sections.title: Why Data Processing, Coding & Tabulation Are Important

blocks.text: Raw data needs to be checked and organised before it can be used to draw conclusions. Errors, duplicate entries or inconsistent responses can affect the quality of research findings.
Proper data processing helps to:
Identify missing, duplicate or inconsistent responses.
Keep data in a clear and consistent format.
Group open-ended answers into useful categories.
Make it easier to compare responses across groups.
Prepare accurate tables and reports for analysis.
Data checking and cleaning
Duplicate and outlier review based on agreed rules
Open-ended response coding
Code-frame development and coding
Variable naming and value labelling
Data formatting and file preparation
Frequency tables and cross-tabulations
Charting and tabulation support
NexGen follows an agreed process to check, organise and prepare research data.
Review the data: We review the questionnaire, dataset and project requirements.
Set processing rules: We agree on data cleaning and exclusion rules before processing.
Check and code responses: We check completeness and consistency and code responses where required.
Process and tabulate: We organise the data and prepare frequency tables and cross-tabulations.
Quality review: We check the processed data and resolve any queries.
Deliver the outputs: We share the final files and supporting documents in the agreed format.

NexGen provides clean Excel or other agreed datasets, code frames, tabulations, processing notes and files ready for analysis. SPSS and other output formats can also be agreed at the start of the project.
